Subject: Proposal: SLA credit for implementation performance + lead handoff

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the call earlier. As discussed, AppScale is excited to pilot a closer commercial alignment for our implementation engagements with Redwood customers. Two asks we want to put on the table so our teams can move quickly:

1) A simple SLA-credit mechanism if our implementation misses agreed delivery windows that materially impact customer production timelines. We think a credit applied to the first invoice (or a one-time service credit) keeps the accounting clean.
2) A clear lead registration and escalation process so our consulting-sourced opportunities are protected and don't get double-credited across channel partners.

I've attached a short draft (draft_revshare_term_v1.docx) that combines a modest 10% revenue-share on services bookings for the first 12 months of a signed deal, with an opt-in "adoption kicker" (one-time bonus payment if usage metrics exceed agreed thresholds in the first 90 days). We included language on a 120-day claim window for lead registration and a mutual-resolution step before applying clawbacks.

Key questions for your team:
- Would Redwood accept the SLA-credit as a capped percentage of the implementation fee (we suggested 15%)?
- Is a 120-day claim window for registration workable? Some of our customers move quickly and some slowly — we want a fair window.
- How would Redwood operationalize the adoption kicker (who verifies metrics, cadence, and payout timing)?

Happy to jump on a quick call this week; otherwise we can iterate in thread.

Thanks,
Elena Park

Thanks Hannah — read through Elena's draft. I have commercial comments below: 

1) Revenue-share and timing: 10% on services for the first 12 months is fine, but we should make payout quarterly and tie payment to invoiced revenue (not projected). Avoid paying on OTE.
2) Clawback window: 120-day registration claim is okay as an exception, but set default to 90 days and allow partners to request extended windows case-by-case (we can capture approval in HubSpot). If we accept 120 days broadly we risk overlap with other partners.
3) Adoption kicker: rename to "usage milestone bonus" and define clear verification (we should require Redwood billing metric or a dashboard export; partner-supplied screenshots are not sufficient). Payout should happen 30 days after verification and subject to no active disputes.
4) SLA-credit cap: 15% max of implementation invoice is acceptable, but credits should be applied to the next Redwood invoice or issued as a service-credit within 30 days. Avoid retroactive cash refunds where possible for bookkeeping.

Operational asks for contract team / legal redlines: remove overly broad confidentiality carve-outs for partners; tighten definitions of "implementation completion" to specific SOW milestones. I'll prepare suggested language and route to legal.

For registration ops: Ben, can you provide the CSV template for partner registrations (fields we need and proof types)? Elena — adding the CSV template as an attachment will speed registration.

Elena / team — operationally this is workable if we run through a short checklist. I'm attaching the registration CSV template (lead_registration_csv_template.csv) and a one-page ops checklist in the repo. Quick ops notes: 

- Registration fields we require: partner_name, partner_contact_email, customer_name, customer_domain, lead_source_date, supporting_evidence_type (email/meeting notes), evidence_reference (HubSpot link or PDF).
- Primary validation: partner must submit registration within claim window and include HubSpot link OR an introductory email chain showing the intro to a Redwood AE.
- Duplicate claims: if another partner has previously submitted the same customer, we escalate to Partner Ops for manual adjudication. Our standard adjudication SLA is 7 business days; if unresolved we move to Senior Partnerships (Hannah + Marissa) for final decision.
- Adoption verification: we can provide a read-only usage export for the 90-day window that includes anonymous usage metrics. For deal-level verification we need the signed customer consent to share billing metrics; we should capture that in the SOW.
- Accounting: revenue-share payable on Redwood invoices only; payment terms net-45 after invoice. Kicker payouts processed on separate vendor invoice after verification.

Next steps: Elena, please confirm the claim window you'd like to proceed with (90 vs 120). Marissa, once your legal redlines are in we can create a DocuSign powerform (linked) and route for signatures. I'll open a Jira ticket for the registration automation (SUP-3241) and add the CSV template to the partner repo.
